gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Wide-stretched wire lettering up top, with Amadeus spacing its curves far from their stems, while Noto Serif Bengali sets a thick band of refined text below. Its hairlines never go razor thin.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-devanag: Noto Serif Devanagari brings a literary text serif with short ascenders and a big lowercase, set under the wirelike, stretched-out Amadeus. Over many lines it settles into a steady, bookish rhythm.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-dives-a: Wide, bold and drawn like wire. Amadeus keeps every stroke uniform, while Noto Serif Dives Akuru adds short capitals among tall small letters and a soft, readable shift in weight through each curve.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Stitched-thread strokes stretch wide across the line in Amadeus, with no tilt to its round letters. Noto Serif Dogra does the quieter work, a classic serif with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-ethiopi: Amadeus joins its strokes at exactly the thickness of the lines themselves, giving wide, commanding words with no tilt. Noto Serif Ethiopic follows as a classic serif whose words sit in solid blocks, softly modulated.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-georgia: Authoritative is the mood of Noto Serif Georgian, tightly coiled lowercase with subdued contrast, set under the wide, bold Amadeus. Noto Serif Georgian is the classic serif counterweight to a heading whose stroke never varies.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-gujarat: Amadeus stretches wide and bold, its letters looking bent from a single wire. Noto Serif Gujarati carries a text serif with oversized e and a counters, and its mild thick-and-thin rhythm keeps pages bookish and unhurried.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-gurmukh: Zero stroke modulation, stretched wide across every word. Amadeus carries the heading, and if it were shrunk down its wire-thin lines would fade, while Noto Serif Gurmukhi, a text serif with a generous x-height, wants the space of body copy.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Noto Serif Kannada reads traditional and literary, with big counters in a tall lowercase and moderate contrast. Amadeus is built for wide, wire-steady display lines, while this classic serif handles the text.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Blueprint lines, stretched wide. Amadeus draws constant strokes with no tilt, and Noto Serif Khmer answers underneath with a tall-lowercase serif whose lighter horizontals never turn threadlike, so heading and text feel firmly authored.
